title: The cap of 2,000 crash reports a day for everyone together is never tested
what: Crash reports are capped at 30 a day from one network address and 2,000 a day for all reports together, to keep the free database from filling. A test checks the 30 cap; nothing checks the 2,000 cap, so a change that broke it would pass.
expected: A test fills the day with 2,000 reports from many addresses and sees the next one refused with 429 and no row saved.
fix_line: Add one test that pre-fills 2,000 reports and checks the next is refused

title: MettleUp's messages in the bell are never tested for staff, for two gyms, or at the 120-day edge
what: The bell test opens 'From MettleUp' only as an owner. No test opens it as staff or checks two gyms see the same messages and nothing of each other. The age test only asks that the limit is at least 90 days and uses a 6-month-old message, so a limit anywhere from 90 to 180 days would pass though the promise is 120.
expected: Tests open the bell as staff, compare two gyms, and check a 119-day message shows while a 121-day one does not.
fix_line: Add a staff bell check and pin the 120-day edge in the server test

title: AI column matching for staff, an ended sign-in and a used-up day is checked only as a status code
what: The server tests check that a staff login gets 403 and an ended key 401, but not that no AI call is made or no read counted for them. No screen test shows the import with the daily limit used up, the demo gym, a staff login, or a person just made owner; the words the owner reads in those cases are never checked.
expected: Server tests check no AI call and no count for staff and an ended key; one screen test per refusal checks the import falls back to matching by hand with its plain line.
fix_line: Assert no AI call and no count on each refusal, and add screen checks for the refusal lines

title: Most of the AI Assistant's refusal words are never checked
what: Only the daily-limit, no-credit and paused words are checked exactly. The words for an empty ask, the demo gym, a too-long voice clip, the trial money cap, a diet-plan ask, too few exercises and too few usable days are checked only by a status or a short piece, and only the no-credit line is checked on a screen. A wording or wiring change in the others would pass.
expected: Each refusal's exact words are checked once on the server, and the cap, demo and too-long lines once on the screen.
fix_line: Assert the exact refusal words in the server tests and add screen checks for three of them

title: Browser alerts are tested only for an owner on the path where everything works
what: The screen test turns alerts on and off for an owner with a working key. Nothing on a screen checks what a person sees when MettleUp has not set up alerts, that a failed browser sign-up never says alerts are on, or a staff member turning alerts on and off.
expected: Screen tests for the not-set-up answer (a plain line, no 'on'), a refused browser sign-up, and a staff login turning alerts on and off.
fix_line: Add three screen checks: not set up, refused sign-up, staff on and off
